cf.title: Docs: Create table description for constraints markup fix and label tweaks

input.subject: Docs: Create table description for constraints markup fix and label tweaks

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. Both patches change only doc/src/sgml/ref/create_table.sgml: 0001 corrects element nesting for UNIQUE and PRIMARY KEY, and 0002 answers a reader report on -general cited in message #1. A reviewer confirmed in message #3 that make html builds. The remaining points are scope and wording choices for a committer.

brief.title: Fix SGML nesting and rename constraint labels in create table docs
brief.problem: In the create table reference page, the UNIQUE and PRIMARY KEY table constraint entries put the INCLUDE clause outside the enclosing literal element. A report on -general also said the labels "(column constraint)" and "(table constraint)" look like the defined syntax names column_constraint and table_constraint, which confuses readers of the syntax area.
brief.proposed_design: Patch 0001 moves the optional INCLUDE clause inside the literal element in the UNIQUE and PRIMARY KEY terms. Patch 0002 adds the word "variant" to the six table and column constraint labels for UNIQUE, PRIMARY KEY and REFERENCES/FOREIGN KEY. Both patches touch only doc/src/sgml/ref/create_table.sgml.
user_visible_surface: Create table reference page: the INCLUDE clause renders inside the literal markup for UNIQUE and PRIMARY KEY table constraints.
Create table reference page: labels change to "(column constraint variant)" and "(table constraint variant)" in six places.
author_claims: The current labels match a defined syntax label, and this confused a user on -general.
Adding "variant" to the labels removes that confusion.
UNIQUE had the same markup error as PRIMARY KEY, so v2 fixes both.
brief.thread_state: The author posted v1 and then v2, which extends the markup fix to UNIQUE. Dapeng Wang reviewed v2, confirmed that make html builds, and said it looks good; no committer has replied.
unclear: The material does not say whether the markup fix should be back-patched, or to which branches.
The author noted inconsistent use of optional markup versus literal brackets but did not say whether that is in scope.
The material does not say whether other reference pages, such as alter table, use the same labels and need the same change.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The CommitFest entry is tagged Bugfix, and the thread does not say whether the 0001 markup fix goes to back branches.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Should the 0001 markup fix be back-patched, and if so to which branches?
Do other reference pages, such as alter table, use the "(column constraint)" and "(table constraint)" labels and need the same change?
Is the inconsistent use of optional markup versus literal brackets, noted in message #2, in scope for this patch set or left for later?
Does the original reporter on -general find that "(column constraint variant)" removes the confusion with the column_constraint syntax name?

committability.owner_note: Any committer who handles documentation patches and knows the reference page markup conventions could take this; none has replied in the thread.
committability.liability: The committer signs for the rendered create table page and for the new "variant" wording, which later readers may ask to see applied on other pages. There is no code, format or behaviour liability.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted v2 on the same day as v1 with a wider fix, which suggests continued attention; there is no reply after the review in message #3.

priority.reason: The two patches are a few lines in one widely read reference page and already have a positive review in message #3. The entry has moved through two CommitFests without a committer reply, so it needs a committer to pick it up.

provisional_note: The documentation hunks were read in full, but the rendered HTML was not seen. Whether "variant" is the best wording, and whether the same labels exist on other pages, could not be checked from the material.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Change a constraint's index - ALTER TABLE ... ALTER CONSTRAINT ... USING INDEX ...
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Tom Lane, Alvaro Herrera, Laurenz Albe
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds ALTER TABLE ... ALTER CONSTRAINT ... USING INDEX to replace the index behind an EXCLUDE, UNIQUE, PRIMARY KEY or FOREIGN KEY constraint with a similar index. The main use case is swapping a primary key index for one with INCLUDE columns, or back.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane wanted the feature rejected because a primary key with a swapped index is no longer an accurate primary key, and information_schema cannot describe it. Alvaro Herrera and Laurenz Albe agreed that primary keys with INCLUDE columns would first need PRIMARY KEY syntax, so that pg_dump works. That leaves this command a narrow use case. The author did not answer the review, and Michael Paquier marked the entry returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
TBH I think if we really wanted the feature of primary keys with
included columns, we'd have to add it to the PRIMARY KEY syntax rather
than having an ad-hoc ALTER TABLE ALTER CONSTRAINT USING INDEX command
to replace the index underneath.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_get_constraintdef: Schema qualify foreign tables unless pretty printing is enabled
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pg_get_constraintdef schema-qualify the referenced table in a foreign key's REFERENCES clause when pretty printing is off, as pg_get_indexdef already does. The goal is constraint definitions that can be recreated on another system with a different search_path.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane said pg_get_indexdef is the odd one out, since most generate_relation_name calls in ruleutils.c ignore the pretty flag, and Alvaro Herrera judged the patch too small for making PRETTYFLAG_SCHEMA work consistently. Tom asked for a clearly defined rule on which call sites qualify names, with a documented helper function. The author did not reply to these reviews, and Michael Paquier returned the patch after six weeks without a reply.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: In other words, I think your patch is too small.

precedents_retrieved.title: Parallel Inserts in CREATE TABLE AS
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets the leader and the parallel workers insert tuples into the new table themselves when the SELECT part of CREATE TABLE AS runs under a top-level Gather node, so no tuples go back through the Gather. A second patch changes the planner to ignore parallel tuple cost for such queries so that it picks parallel plans more often.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the patch after measuring a regression with large tuples (about 1064 bytes). Workers extending the relation at the same time spent most of their time in RelationAddExtraBlocks flushing new empty pages to disk. A reviewer measured about 6% degradation in that case. The author proposed waiting for faster relation extension, such as fallocate() from the AIO/DIO work.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Upon
further analysis, it turned out that the parallel workers are
requiring frequent extra blocks addition while concurrently extending
the relation(in RelationAddExtraBlocks) and the majority of the time
spent is going into flushing those new empty pages/blocks onto the
disk.

precedents_retrieved.title: create table like: ACCESS METHOD
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Peter Eisentraut, Michael Paquier, Vik Fearing
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add an ACCESS METHOD option to CREATE TABLE ... LIKE, so that INCLUDING ACCESS METHOD (and INCLUDING ALL) copies the source table's table access method to the new table. Partitioned tables would silently ignore the option.
precedents_retrieved.objection: LIKE expands to column definitions, but the access method is a table property, so two LIKE clauses with different access methods can conflict. Its interaction with USING is also undefined. The patch overwrote any AM given in USING, and Michael Paquier asked for a clear definition of these corner cases. Peter Eisentraut argued that this syntax is the wrong approach and suggested something like USING (LIKE t1).
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Whereas the access method is a table property.  So I don't think this syntax is the right approach for this feature.

precedents_retrieved.title: [PROPOSAL] : Disallow use of empty column name in (column_name '') in ALTER or CREATE of foreign table.
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes postgres_fdw's validator reject empty values for the column_name, schema_name and table_name options in create or alter foreign table. Today an empty column_name is accepted, and the remote query then fails with a zero-length identifier error.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane judged that the check did not add enough ease-of-use to justify the extra code, and he compared an empty name to a misspelled remote name, which cannot be checked either. Robert Haas pointed out that existing foreign tables with empty values would then fail pg_dump or pg_upgrade. Nobody argued for the patch after Tom voted against it, so Robert marked it Rejected.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I was down on it to start with, on the grounds that it wasn't adding enough ease-of-use to justify even a relatively small amount of added code.

precedents_retrieved.title: Document creating an extension in replication setup
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds documentation on how to set up extensions in a physical replication setup: shared_preload_libraries and related settings must be configured on primary and standbys, while CREATE EXTENSION runs only on the primary and is replicated. Version 3 moved the text to high-availability.sgml and spoke of modules in general.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Julien Rouhaud's review of v3 found the wording confusing and partly wrong, and the visible messages show no later version. He said the text does not make clear that a preloaded library is needed on a standby only if it should be enabled there, including after promotion. He also said the text wrongly ties the need for preloading to whether the module exposes SQL functions.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The need for preloading is entirely orthogonal
to SQL functions in the extension, especially since this is implying SQL
function over C-code.

precedents_retrieved.title: Replace literal 0 values with the appropriate Invalid* constants
precedents_retrieved.summary: Replace literal 0 values with the matching Invalid* constants (InvalidMultiXactId, InvalidOffsetNumber, InvalidAttrNumber, InvalidDsaPointer, InvalidRelFileNumber) across about 30 files. A Coccinelle script generated the changes, following the earlier InvalidXLogRecPtr cleanup in ec317440716.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund objected that such wholesale cleanup patches add more noise than they improve the code and use review bandwidth better spent elsewhere. He said these changes are fine when the code is edited for other reasons. The author agreed the changes add little value and withdrew the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think we should reject these and other similar patches, they generate way
more noise than they are improving the code.

precedents_retrieved.title: clean up create|alter domain stmt incompatiable constraint error case and add regression test
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch added broader regression tests for CREATE DOMAIN and ALTER DOMAIN (DefineDomain had low test coverage) and cleaned up error handling for incompatible domain constraints. It replaced the unhelpful "unrecognized constraint subtype" error for generated-column constraints on domains with a clear message, and made ALTER DOMAIN ... ADD CONSTRAINT ... NO INHERIT NOT VALID fail.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The entry was withdrawn because the patch had been folded into a later patch version (v6) in another thread. A reviewer asked whether this separate commitfest entry should therefore be closed. No objection to the content of the patch is shown.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Looks like this patch is now part of v6 from here [0]. Should we close
[1] CF entry?

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P19] is about consistency of server application synopses, and [P10] is about making join syntax more prominent on the select page. Neither records a reason that applies to a markup nesting fix or a label change on the create table page. The thread does not mention an earlier attempt at this change.

This is a docs-only change to create_table.sgml, with no change to SQL syntax, GUCs, pg_dump, psql or client behaviour. The markup fix aligns UNIQUE and PRIMARY KEY with how their syntax is written, and the "variant" wording conflicts with no existing term. Other pages such as alter_table.sgml may use the same labels, but that is a follow-up question, not a failure.

Both patches change only doc/src/sgml/ref/create_table.sgml. They add no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog entry, protocol message or extension API, so nothing in this proposal is persistent or crosses a process or machine boundary.

The patch changes only markup and label text on the create table reference page. It adds nothing that affects privileges, authentication, data exposure or resource use, so the security angle has no objection.

From the maintenance and fit angle there is nothing to object to. The patches change only doc/src/sgml/ref/create_table.sgml, add no mechanism, GUC, API or hot-path cost, and leave no future feature with a new place to update. The markup fix corrects a real nesting error, and a reviewer confirmed that make html builds. Open points such as back-patching and other reference pages are scope questions for a committer to decide.
This is a docs-only fix to markup and labels on the create table page. No existing feature, option, extension or tool already does this, so the already-exists angle has no objection to raise.

Demand is shown for a docs-only fix. Patch 0001 corrects malformed markup, which needs no demand case. Patch 0002 answers a concrete reader report on -general (message #1), costs nothing on any hot path, and touches one reference page. Whether "variant" is the best wording is a question for other angles.
